Here is the commit message:
ASoC: meson: aiu: fix irq registration

The aiu stored the irq in an unsigned integer which may have discarded an
error returned by platform_get_irq_byname(). This is incorrect and should
have been a signed integer.

Also drop the irq error traces from the probe function as this is already
done by platform_get_irq_byname().

Fixes: 6ae9ca9ce986 ("ASoC: meson: aiu: add i2s and spdif support")
Reported-by: kbuild test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Jerome Brunet <jbrunet@baylibre.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200214131350.337968-4-jbrunet@baylibre.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by storing the IRQ value in an unsigned integer, which could lead to the loss of negative error values returned by the `platform_get_irq_byname()` function. This incorrect type handling meant that any error indicating a failure to retrieve the IRQ would be discarded, potentially leading to undefined behavior or crashes when the code attempted to use an invalid IRQ value.

Here is the patch:
 	struct clk_bulk_data *clks;
 	unsigned int clk_num;
-	unsigned int irq;
+	int irq;
 };

When `platform_get_irq_byname()` returns a negative error code (indicating failure), this value is incorrectly stored in the `irq` variable, leading to the loss of the error information. Consequently, the code may attempt to use an invalid IRQ value, resulting in undefined behavior or crashes.

irq = platform_get_irq_byname(...);
